sections.title: The Institutional Formula: -ásra/-ésre kerül
sections.content: In Hungarian administrative, judicial, and corporate communication, the periphrasis formed by a verbal noun (ending in -ás/-és) + sublative case suffix (-ra/-re) + the verb 'kerül' serves as the primary formal surrogate for passive constructions: 'A javaslat elfogadásra került' (The proposal was adopted), 'Az új szabályzat bevezetésre kerül' (The new policy will be introduced).

sections.title: Syntactic Agreement and Communicative Function
sections.content: The verb 'kerül' inflects normally for tense and number according to the grammatical subject: 'A határozatok elfogadásra kerültek' (plural past). While stylistic purists caution against its overuse in creative prose, mastering this structure is indispensable for understanding government decrees ('határozat'), legal statutes, and diplomatic communiqués where the agency of the decision-maker is deliberately backgrounded.

items.spanish: Az új törvényjavaslat a parlamentben egyhangúlag elfogadásra került.
items.english: The new bill was unanimously adopted in parliament.

items.spanish: A tervezett intézkedések a jövő hónapban bevezetésre kerülnek.
items.english: The planned measures will be implemented next month.

items.spanish: A minisztérium határozatban rögzítette a döntést.
items.english: The ministry recorded the decision in a decree.

items.spanish: A polgárok beadványa sajnos elutasításra került a hivatalban.
items.english: The citizens' petition was unfortunately rejected at the office.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Pay close attention to vowel harmony: back-vowel stems take '-ásra kerül' (pl. 'elfogadásra'), while front-vowel stems take '-ésre kerül' (pl. 'bevezetésre').
